question: A man sold an article for ₹222, there by gaining 20%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fractional equivalent of 20% profit = +1/5

This means if Cost Price (CP) is 5 parts, Profit is 1 part, and Selling Price (SP) is 6 parts.

Given SP (6 parts) = ₹222

Value of 1 part = 222 ÷ 6 = ₹37

Cost Price (5 parts) = 5 × 37 = ₹185

**∴ The correct answer is ₹185.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹222

Profit = 20%

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 Cost Price
 CP = ?
 
 
 Selling Price
 SP = ₹222
 
 

 +20% Profit
 
 CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + P%)

**Formula Used:**

CP = [SP × 100] ÷ (100 + Profit%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ CP = (222 × 100) ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ CP = 22200 ÷ 120

⇒ CP = 2220 ÷ 12

⇒ CP = 185

**∴ The correct answer is ₹185.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Scenario

When an article is sold at a loss, the Cost Price is calculated as: CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Loss%).

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Percentage Change

Net effect of two successive changes A% and B% is given by: A + B + (A × B) ÷ 100.
